newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by outlooks for continued heavy marketings, livestock dealers said.

Marketings were expected to remain hefty following a spring snowstorm late last week that delayed hog movement, they said. Now with temperatures warming and snow melting, producers were trying to get marketings caught up before they resumed fieldwork, the dealers said.
"We've already got a few tractors back in the fields," one central Indiana hog buyer said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts on Monday were estimated at 110,000 head, up 5,000 from a week ago and a year ago, USDA statistics showed.
Interior marketings on Friday were 108,000 head, down 2,000 from the estimate, but Saturday's were 34,000, up 19,000 from the estimate.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range $54.50 to $55.00 and in Illinois could span $53.00 to $53.50.
Indiana/Ohio top plant prices could range $53.50 to $54.00, the dealers said.
